problem: Single-agent EQA methods (e.g. Explore Until Confident) run independently in multi-robot settings, causing redundant exploration. Naive LLM-based communication is miscalibrated and overconfident, so shared messages can be irrelevant or misleading.
motivation: Future households will have heterogeneous robots with non-transferable assignments who can still share observations to speed up information gathering. Messages must be accurate and relevant to the receiver's tasks, otherwise they hurt efficiency. The paper argues an agent should only communicate information it is confident is relevant to its partner's task.
key_idea: Each robot uses an LLM to judge whether its observed objects are the partner's target (A) or relevant to it (B), and uses conformal prediction on the option probabilities to filter these into calibrated natural-language messages that bias the partner's semantic-value frontier exploration.
insight: Ablations show calibration matters: Ours-No-CP performs about like the non-communicating MMEuC, and Ours-Com-Control, which sends as many but random objects, also fails to help, so message quality matters more than quantity. Answer sharing further reduces NTC, and the advantage over MMFBE grows with scene size (NTC improvement of 0.6 in the largest scenes).
method: Perception: a VLM (Prismatic-VLM-13B) lists observed objects with colors from the RGB image.

Object relevance reasoning: LLaMA3-8B-instruct with zero-shot CoT chooses among options A (same as the request), B (relevant/co-located), C (unrelated), D (common feature) for each observed/requested object pair, and the option token probability is taken as the score.

Conformal message generation: split CP with separate calibration sets for A and B, built from 20 HM3D scenes; thresholds are the 0.6 quantile for A and 0.82 for B. Objects passing the threshold fill a template message with object positions; if none pass, no message is sent.

Communication-aware semantic map: the received counts of relevant and target objects give SV_com = log(τ1·Num_rel + τ2·Num_tgt) with τ1=1 and τ2=10. It is combined with the agent's own SV by max, averaged over questions, Gaussian-smoothed, and used with TSDF mapping and frontier-based exploration.
Confidence check and answer sharing: an answer is accepted if a unique option has Ans×Rel > 1-ε2. Confident answers to a partner's question are sent to that partner.
Stop criterion: a robot stops when all its questions are answered, by itself or by partners, or when Tmax is reached.

setting.backbone: Prismatic-VLM-13B (frozen) for perception and confidence; LLaMA3-8B-instruct (frozen, temperature 0.7) for communication reasoning
setting.training_data: none (training-free); a calibration set of (observed, target) object pairs from 20 HM3D scenes is used for conformal prediction
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + pose, per robot
setting.action_space: frontier-based navigation to target positions via a collision-free planner (waypoint-level), robot speed 1 m/s
setting.privileged: none at test time (calibration uses ground-truth labels from 20 separate scenes)

numbers.eval_set_note: 70 scenes, 420 question tasks (2 robots x 3 questions per scene)
numbers.extra: message speed 1 msg/s, robot speed 1 m/s; SR/NTC read from the text describing the curve; the 445 s figure is average completion time
numbers.evidence: "achieving an SR of 0.68 at an NTC of 0.4, compared to MMFBE's SR of 0.65 at an NTC of 0.8"; "'Ours' completes all questions in an average of 445 seconds, compared to 594 seconds for MMFBE"

numbers_note: Results are mostly given as SR-vs-NTC curves in figures; only a few numbers appear in the text and no result tables exist. The MM-EQA benchmark is the paper's own, so it is listed under other.
results: CommCP reaches an SR of 0.68 at an NTC of 0.4, whereas the strongest baseline MMFBE reaches 0.65 at an NTC of 0.8 (roughly 2x efficiency). Average completion time is 445 s versus 594 s for MMFBE. It also gets the highest final SR, and its benefit grows with scene size and holds with 3 robots and varying message latencies.
limitations: Uses a small open-source LLM (LLaMA3-8B) because token probabilities are required, so stronger closed models cannot be used.
Evaluated only in simulation, with 2-3 robots and one self-built benchmark; the i.i.d./exchangeability assumption is argued rather than verified, and the coverage guarantee is only marginal.
Results are mostly shown as curves without tables, and the coverage level is tuned via hand-set quantiles (0.6 and 0.82).
builds_on: KnowNo / conformal prediction for robot planning
